answer: A new identity starts on a tundra of isolation: it may bid for work, but its votes and settlement claims stay inert until a lagoon of completed jobs with already-established, unlinked counterparties has been independently attested under one custody key. Those jobs are written into a public atlas bound to that key; merging two keys mid-era voids both maps. A farm therefore cannot share one work history across aliases, and cannot cash influence until each identity has paid its own isolation time.
